question: India has unveiled a comprehensive plan worth ₹ 9.15 lakh crore (US$ 109.50 billion) to enhance its power infrastructure and meet a projected demand of 458 GW by ________.
solution:
The Correct answer is __**2032**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India has outlined a comprehensive plan worth **₹9.15 lakh crore** (equivalent to **US$109.50 billion**) to strengthen its power infrastructure.
 
• This plan aims to meet the projected power demand of **458 GW** by the year **2032**.
 
• The initiative focuses on enhancing the country’s **power generation capacity**, modernizing **transmission networks**, and ensuring **energy security**.
 
• The government intends to achieve this target by leveraging **renewable energy sources** such as **solar, wind, and hydroelectric power**.
 
• This development aligns with India’s commitments under the **Paris Agreement** to reduce **carbon emissions** and transition towards a **clean energy economy**.
 
• The initiative is also expected to bolster **economic growth**, create **employment opportunities**, and ensure **universal electricity access**.
 
• In 2023, India’s installed power generation capacity stands at approximately **417.68 GW**, indicating significant progress towards the 2032 target.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Key focus areas under this plan:**__

 __
 
• Development of **green energy corridors** to integrate renewable energy into the national grid.
 
• Upgrading **distribution infrastructure** to reduce power losses.
 
• Promoting **energy storage technologies** such as **batteries** to ensure grid reliability.
 
• Encouraging **private sector investments** in the energy sector.
 
 
 
• **Global Comparison:**__
 
 
• India’s power infrastructure development plan is one of the largest globally, reflecting its position as the **third-largest energy consumer** in the world.
 
• Countries like **China and the USA** have also implemented similar large-scale infrastructure programs to meet their growing energy demands.
